modal.title: Connect to {client}
modal.runCommand: Run this command in your terminal:
modal.cursorBody: Click the button below to automatically add this MCP server to Cursor. Cursor must be installed on your machine.
modal.vscodeBody: Click the button below to automatically add this MCP server to VS Code. GitHub Copilot extension required for MCP support.
modal.copilotBody: GitHub Copilot supports remote MCP servers in VS Code, Visual Studio (desktop), JetBrains, Eclipse and Xcode. Add the config below to the matching file for your IDE, then start the server from the Copilot Chat → Tools menu.
modal.copilotVscode: VS Code: workspace .vscode/mcp.json (or use the one-click button below).
modal.copilotOther: JetBrains / Eclipse / Xcode: Copilot Chat → MCP settings → add server, paste the endpoint URL.
modal.apiKeyInstead: Using an API key instead of OAuth?
modal.claudeWebStep1: 1. Click the button below: Claude opens its Add custom connector dialog.
modal.claudeWebStep2: 2. Enter a name and paste the MCP endpoint URL below, then click Add.
modal.claudeWebFallback: Dialog not showing? In Claude open Customize → Connectors, click +, then Add custom connector.
modal.claudeDesktopRecommended: Recommended: add this server from Claude Desktop's built-in connector settings — it runs the OAuth login for you, with no file editing. Editing claude_desktop_config.json with a remote URL does not work: that file only launches local commands, so Claude skips it as “not a valid MCP server configuration”.
modal.claudeDesktopStep1: 1. Open Customize → Connectors (in Claude Desktop, or with the button below).
modal.claudeDesktopStep3: 3. Enter a name and paste the MCP endpoint URL below, then click Add.
modal.bridgeSummary: Prefer the config file? Use the mcp-remote bridge
modal.bridgeBody: Requires Node.js. The mcp-remote package wraps the remote server as a local command. Add to claude_desktop_config.json and restart Claude Desktop.
modal.chatgptStep1: 1. Click the button below to open Plugins in ChatGPT, then click + and Add custom MCP server.
modal.chatgptStep2: 2. Enter a name (e.g. AnythingMCP), paste the MCP endpoint URL below as the Server URL and keep Authentication on OAuth.
modal.chatgptStep3: 3. Select I understand and want to continue, then Create as a plugin, and sign in to AnythingMCP when asked.
modal.chatgptStep4: 4. Install the plugin from your personal plugins, then type @ in a chat to use it.
modal.chatgptNote: No developer mode needed. On a Business workspace only admins and owners can add custom MCP servers; on Enterprise and Edu an admin can grant the Create plugins with MCPs permission under Workspace settings → Permissions & roles.
modal.museStep1: 1. In Meta Muse, open Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector.
modal.museStep2: 2. Paste the MCP endpoint URL below.
modal.museStep3: 3. Muse opens the AnythingMCP sign-in page: sign in and approve access.
modal.museStep4: 4. Ask Muse to use one of the tools.
modal.museChat: Or paste this into a Muse chat (web, iOS, Android or WhatsApp):
modal.museNote: Meta does not review custom connectors; you can disconnect this one any time in Muse under Settings → Connectors. Muse is currently available in the US and Canada only.
modal.inspectorRun: Run this command in your terminal (Node 22.19 or later). It starts the Inspector already pointed at this server:
modal.inspectorOpens: The Inspector opens in your browser. If it doesn't, open it here:
modal.inspectorToken: The Inspector hands its session token (MCP_INSPECTOR_API_TOKEN) to the page it opens, so you don't need to copy it.
modal.inspectorAuth: Sign in with OAuth when the Inspector asks (connect, sign in and approve access), or use an API key: set an X-API-Key header in the server's settings in the Inspector. You can also add {headerFlag} to the command, but the key then stays in your shell history.

connectorNew.mcpUrlHint: Paste the complete MCP endpoint URL including its path — e.g. a Snowflake managed server at <mono>{example}</mono>. A bare host with no path defaults to <mono>{fallback}</mono>.

odata.sapHint: The base URL is the SAP host; services are found through SAP's service catalog. Leave unticked for a single OData service, with its service root as the base URL.
odata.toolsHint: The connector comes with tools to list services, read their fields and labels, query entity sets and read single entities. Specific tools per entity set can be imported from $metadata afterwards.

database.readOnlyHint: Only SELECT queries will be allowed. Safe for analytics and reporting.
database.readWriteHint: All SQL operations (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) will be allowed. Use with caution.

spec.hint: Provide a spec URL to auto-generate MCP tools.

oauth.passwordRequired: Enter the username and password the password grant sends to the token URL.
oauth.mcpHint: After creating the connector, you will be redirected to authorize with the remote MCP server via OAuth. Tools will be discovered automatically after authorization.
oauth.grantCode: Authorization code (sign in at the provider)
oauth.passwordHint: For APIs that issue tokens with no refresh token: a new one is requested with the username and password whenever it expires. Datto RMM: username = API key, password = API secret, client ID public-client, secret public, HTTP Basic.
oauth.tokenAuthMachineHint: How the client ID and secret reach the token URL.
oauth.tokenAuthHint: Switch to HTTP Basic if the provider returns 401 when exchanging the code — DATEV requires it. Applies to token refreshes too.
oauth.machineHint: No sign-in needed: the connector requests its access token from the token URL, and a new one whenever it expires.
oauth.redirectHint: After creating the connector, you will be redirected to authorize via OAuth2. Tokens will be stored securely.
oauth.callback: Set the Redirect / Callback URI in your OAuth provider to:

apiKey.headerInvalid: The HTTP header the key is sent in, e.g. X-API-Key: letters, digits and - only, no spaces.

wsSecurity.hint: Sent as a wsse:Security UsernameToken in the SOAP header. PasswordDigest sends a hash of the password with a nonce and timestamp instead of the password itself.

loginToken.invalidJson: Login body must be valid JSON.
loginToken.intro: For APIs with short-lived tokens (e.g. HRworks): we POST your credentials to the login endpoint, read the token from the response, send it as a Bearer token, and refresh it automatically before it expires.
loginToken.bodyHint: Body sent to the login URL. Use {user} / {pass} placeholders. HRworks uses {example}.
loginToken.refreshOn401: Re-login and retry automatically on a 401 response

catalog.installedFrom: This connector was installed from {slug}, which has changed since.
catalog.provenanceUser: This address was changed here, not by the catalog — a region, a sandbox or a self-hosted instance. Applying this will undo that.

details.title: Connector Details
details.name: Name
details.healthcheckHint: Path used by "Test connection". Set to an endpoint that returns 2xx without auth (e.g. /health) if the API has no root handler.
details.readOnlyHint: Only SELECT queries are allowed. Safe for analytics and reporting.
details.readWriteHint: All SQL operations (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) are allowed. Use with caution.
details.deniedHint: Queries that name one of these tables are refused. Comma-separated; * matches any text, ? one character, # one digit. The database user's own permissions remain the real boundary.
details.sapHint: Services come from SAP's service catalog; sap-client and sap-language are sent with every request.
details.servicesHint: One service path per line, * as wildcard. Empty allows every service the technical user can call.
details.headerInvalid: The HTTP header the key is sent in, e.g. X-API-Key: letters, digits and - only, no spaces.
details.wsHint: Sent as a wsse:Security UsernameToken in the SOAP header. The password type is saved with the username and password: re-enter both to change it.
details.keepCredentials: Leave credential fields empty to keep the current values.
details.instructionsPlaceholder: Instructions sent to AI clients when using this connector's tools (e.g. date formats, field values, API conventions).
details.instructionsHint: Sent via MCP protocol to help AI understand how to use this connector.

oauth.grantCode: Authorization code (sign in at the provider)
oauth.grantCodeHint: Authorize with Provider once; the refresh token renews the access token.
oauth.grantPasswordHint: For APIs that issue tokens with no refresh token: a new one is requested with the username and password whenever it expires. Datto RMM: username = API key, password = API secret, client public-client / public with HTTP Basic.
oauth.grantClientHint: The client ID and secret alone get the token, and a new one whenever it expires. No sign-in at the provider.
oauth.privateKeyJwt: Signed JWT with your private key (private_key_jwt)
oauth.privateKeyJwtHint: Set by the connector: a short-lived JWT signed with the private key from the environment variables replaces the client secret.
oauth.machineHint: How the client ID and secret reach the token URL. HTTP Basic is the default for this grant.
oauth.basicHint: Switch to HTTP Basic if the token exchange fails with 401 — Datto RMM and DATEV require it. Applies to refreshes too. Re-authorize after changing it.
oauth.pkceHint: On by default. Turn it off only if the provider refuses PKCE: LinkedIn's standard web flow answers 401 invalid_client to it. Re-authorize after changing it.
oauth.keepNote: Leave Client ID / Client Secret empty to keep the stored values. Endpoints are shown as configured and can be corrected here — useful when a connector was switched to OAuth2 after creation and has none yet.

oauth1.noteStored: The consumer key and secret belong to the application registered with the provider — not your login e-mail or password. Leave a field empty to keep the stored value; stored values are never shown. The access token is only for APIs that act on behalf of a user (three-legged).
oauth1.noteNew: The consumer key and secret belong to the application registered with the provider — not your login e-mail or password. Both are required to switch to OAuth 1.0a. The access token is only for APIs that act on behalf of a user (three-legged).

loginToken.intro: For APIs with short-lived tokens (e.g. HRworks): we POST your credentials to the login endpoint, read the token from the response, send it as a Bearer token, and refresh it automatically before it expires. Re-enter the password/secret to change this configuration; leave it empty to keep the current one.
loginToken.refreshOn401: Re-login and retry automatically on a 401 response

toolEditor.name: Tool Name

toolEditor.descriptionPlaceholder: Fetch a list of users with optional filtering
toolEditor.descriptionHint: Clear description helps the AI decide when to use this tool
toolEditor.staticPlaceholder:
# Instructions

Describe how to use this tool or provide hardcoded information.

Markdown formatting is supported.
toolEditor.staticHint: This text is returned directly without making any API call. Use it for instructions, documentation, or hardcoded responses.
toolEditor.graphqlHint: Use $variables in the query — map them to parameters below as "GraphQL Variable"
toolEditor.sqlHint: Use $param_name to reference parameters. Only SELECT queries are allowed.
toolEditor.soapHint: The SOAP operation/method name from the WSDL
toolEditor.pathHint: Use {example} for path parameters — they auto-create parameters below
toolEditor.invalidJson: Not valid JSON — saving is disabled until this parses.
toolEditor.bodyMappingHint: Sent as the request body, structure preserved. Use $param for tool arguments and {connectorVar} / {contextVar} for connector and caller-context values. Shown automatically when the stored mapping is nested — editing it here keeps it intact.
toolEditor.bodyTemplateHint: Use {example} for dynamic values. All other fields are sent as-is. Parameters are auto-extracted below.

params.title: Input Parameters
params.hint: Define what the AI model can pass to this tool, and where each value goes in the API request

params.envTitle: This parameter is auto-filled from an environment variable and hidden from the AI

toolEditor.cacheHint: Cache identical requests in Redis to reduce API calls. Common values: 60 (1 min), 300 (5 min), 3600 (1 hour).

responseMapping.title: Response Mapping
responseMapping.intro: Shape the API response before it reaches the AI client. Fewer tokens, and only the fields this tool actually needs leave your workspace. Off = the raw response is returned unchanged.
responseMapping.invalidJson: Not valid JSON — saving is disabled until this parses.
responseMapping.selectHint: Keys are the output names. A leaf is a path ($.a.b, items[*].id, list[-1].x), a static value ("= my-source"), or {reshape} to reshape every element of an array. A path that does not resolve is left out.
responseMapping.excludeHint: Removed before the template runs. Use this alone (no template) to drop a few noisy fields while keeping everything else.
responseMapping.expressionHint: Full JMESPath, including functions — use this for computed values such as length(devices) or filters like {filter}.
responseMapping.fallback: Fall back to the raw response if the mapping fails
responseMapping.previewTitle: Runs the mapping against the most recent real response for this tool. No API call is made.
responseMapping.previewTitleDisabled: Save the tool and run it once to get a real response to preview against.
responseMapping.mappingFailed: Mapping failed ({error}) — the raw response is shown.

readOnlyHint.label: Read-only
readOnlyHint.help: The tool cannot change anything. Agents probe read-only tools much more freely — set this for searches exposed over POST.

destructiveHint.label: Destructive
destructiveHint.help: The write removes or overwrites data, rather than only adding to it. Only meaningful when the tool is not read-only.

idempotentHint.label: Idempotent
idempotentHint.help: Calling it again with the same arguments changes nothing further. Only meaningful when the tool is not read-only.

openWorldHint.label: Open world
openWorldHint.help: Talks to an external system whose contents we cannot bound. False for a database or a static payload.

toolAnnotations.intro: Hints MCP clients read before calling this tool — most importantly whether it is read-only. They are inferred from the connector; override them only when the inference is wrong (typically a read-only search exposed over POST).

kg.label: Knowledge Graph
kg.description: Auto-discovers relationships between your connectors' entities (from tool definitions and real usage) and exposes them to agents. Disabling it stops graph building, hides the page, and removes the MCP helper tool.

llm.label: AI enrichment
llm.description: Let an LLM suggest extra relationships the heuristics miss (e.g. that a CRM person, a billing customer and a support user are the same person). Only entity and field names are sent — never your data. Suggestions await your confirmation. May incur model costs.

edgeAutoApply.label: Auto-apply high-confidence connections
edgeAutoApply.description: When AI enrichment suggests a connection it is confident about (≥ 0.90), add it to the graph automatically instead of leaving it for manual review. Lower-confidence links still wait for your confirmation. No extra model cost — it only changes how existing suggestions are handled.

captureIntent.label: Capture user intent
captureIntent.description: Adds an optional parameter to every MCP tool asking the agent for the user's original request. Captures the context behind each call so the graph can be optimized and skills suggested over time. This is the default for every user: override it per user under Settings → Users (Skill learning), and each user can opt out in their own settings.

autoExtend.label: Scheduled AI extension
autoExtend.description: On a schedule (roughly daily), let the AI extend the graph and generate skills from the captured user intents — so your network and skills keep improving on their own. Cost-careful: it only runs every so often, skips when nothing changed, and stays off until you enable it. Requires AI enrichment + Capture user intent.

skillAutoApply.label: Auto-apply high-confidence skills
skillAutoApply.description: When AI generates a skill it is confident about (≥ 0.90), apply it automatically instead of leaving it as a suggestion to review. Lower-confidence skills still wait for manual approval.

security.title: Security
security.body: Sign every member out of the dashboard and of every connected AI client, including clients that hold a refresh token. Nobody loses their role or access; everyone simply has to sign in again. Use it after a suspected credential leak or a change in your identity provider. MCP API keys are not sessions and are left alone unless you say otherwise.
